purpose: Real project inputs for adapter integration; this manifest is not an engine evidence manifest or a verdict.

workload.domain: Byte arrays up to 4096 elements; count unordered equal-value index pairs.
workload.frequencies: Equal weights are fixture declarations, not observed production frequencies.

hypothesis: Replace repeated pair comparisons with a 256-bin histogram on a profile-attributed count_pairs hot path. No improvement is guaranteed without measurement.
correctness: Independent fixed examples: empty, singleton, distinct values, mixed 0/255, 100 repeated values, complete byte alphabet. The driver also checks native/Node workload checksums.

transformation.method: Replace only kernel source in the materialized project. Keep harness, cases, flags and correctness tests identical.
transformation.scope: Algorithmic optimization fixture; representative of duplicate counting, not every language ecosystem.

toolchain_policy.rust: rustc with edition 2021 and std::hint::black_box (1.66+); exact version recorded at execution
toolchain_policy.c: C11 compiler; exact version recorded at execution
toolchain_policy.cpp: C++17 compiler; exact version recorded at execution
toolchain_policy.go: 1.24+; GOTOOLCHAIN=local; exact version recorded at execution
toolchain_policy.javascript: Node 24.x, normal JIT; exact version recorded at execution
toolchain_policy.valgrind: installed version recorded; no automatic native support claim

artifacts.retention: Caller-owned output directory, never committed. Do not treat smoke timings as acceptance.

limitations: Fixture checks do not run the shared engine or assign policy verdicts.
Timing requires an explicit engine policy before automatic evaluation.
Native profile routes require successful Linux x86_64 runs for every language, toolchain and route.
No synthetic measurements are supplied. Missing-profile and no-candidate scenarios are input mutations for the engine test consumer.
Driver timeouts bound individual fixture commands; the engine owns experiment limits, isolation and credential policy.
prepare creates source files only; the driver does not commit candidate sources or create branches. The engine owns immutable source revision tracking.
